context.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening is a cloud-native system that screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst review cases. It operates within a mid-size payment processor infrastructure to protect merchant revenue while enforcing security mandates.

## Key Elements
- Shopper / Cardholder
- Merchant
- Fraud Analyst
- Risk / Compliance Officer
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (Target)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External)
- Card Networks / Identity Providers (External)
- Compliance & Audit Archival Storage (External)
- Identity Provider / IdP (External)
- Notification / Alerting Service (External)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to Fraud Screening System via REST/gRPC using mTLS for authorization requests and synchronous decisions
- Fraud Screening System to Compliance & Audit Storage via TLS for immutable log streaming
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Officers to Fraud Screening System via HTTPS/OIDC/SAML through IdP
- Fraud Screening System to Notification Service via HTTPS/SMTP for operational alerts

## Technology Stack
- AWS eu-west-1: Target cloud provider and single region deployment for budget control
- Amazon ECS Fargate / AWS Lambda: Container and serverless compute ensuring minimal infrastructure management for a 3-engineer team
- AWS S3 Object Lock: WORM storage tier guaranteeing 7-year tamper-evident audit log retention
- AWS Secrets Manager: Automated credential and secret rotation
- Terraform / AWS CDK: Infrastructure as Code and GitOps pipeline tooling

## Rationale
Managed AWS services eliminate operational overhead, allowing a 3-engineer team to maintain high availability and sub-50ms latency within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Strict single-region architecture, tokenization, and WORM storage satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability mandates.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-time payment fraud screening system for card-not-present transactions.
- Provides sub-50ms latency scoring, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident audit logging.

## Key Elements
- Shopper / Cardholder & Merchant (External)
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress & Tokenization Boundary)
- Scoring Engine (Rust service on Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Case Management App (Node.js/Python backend on ECS Fargate)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis & Amazon DynamoDB)
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & Kinesis Firehose)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- External IdP (OAuth2/OIDC for analyst authentication)

## Relationships
- Shopper to AWS API Gateway via REST/JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway to Scoring Engine via internal ALB / gRPC
- Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache and DynamoDB via TCP/TLS
- Case Management App to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams via HTTPS
- Kinesis Firehose to Amazon S3 via AWS internal storage APIs
- Analysts to Case Management App via OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Low-overhead HTTP/2 ingress and edge tokenization boundary for PAN data
- Amazon ECS (Fargate): Serverless container orchestration for lightweight operational footprint
- Rust (Tokio): High-performance, low-latency execution for the real-time scoring engine
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): In-memory caching for low-latency feature lookups (<50ms P99)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year compliance audit log storage
- AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Data encryption at rest and secure credential management

## Rationale
- Decouples real-time scoring from asynchronous case management to protect sub-50ms latency under high load.
- Uses serverless ECS Fargate and managed AWS services to satisfy strict cost, security, and compliance requirements within a 3-engineer team capacity.

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size payment processors to detect fraud before approval, while providing case management for suspicious payments. It operates within a strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance framework and a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Shopper / Cardholder & Merchant (External Users)
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress and Tokenization Boundary Container)
- Scoring Engine & Case Management App (Amazon ECS Fargate Containers)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis, Amazon DynamoDB)
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Kinesis Firehose)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- HTTP Route Resolver, Native JWT Authorizer, and VPC Link Integration (AWS API Gateway Components)

## Relationships
- Shopper / Cardholder & Merchant -> HTTP Route Resolver: Sends screening payloads [REST/JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- HTTP Route Resolver -> Native JWT Authorizer: Validates bearer tokens [Internal Evaluation]
- HTTP Route Resolver -> VPC Link Integration: Forwards sanitized payloads [gRPC over HTTP/2]
- VPC Link Integration -> Scoring Engine: Routes screened requests [Internal ALB / gRPC with mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway (HTTP API v2): Provides low-overhead HTTP/2 ingress to meet P99 latency targets.
- API Gateway Native JWT Authorizer: Validates tokens at the edge without custom compute overhead.
- AWS WAF: Deployed at the edge for OWASP protection and DDoS mitigation.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs containerized internal workloads with minimal operational burden.
- Amazon S3 (Object Lock): Secures tamper-evident 7-year audit logs in Compliance Mode.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed cloud services to minimize operational overhead for a three-person engineering team. It enforces low-latency, secure data processing to meet strict performance and PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints within budget.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under strict latency constraints before approval. It simultaneously provides case management for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions safely and efficiently.

## Key Elements
- Ingress Coordinator (Rust `tonic`/`axum`)
- Feature Assembler (`redis-rs`, Amazon ElastiCache Redis, Amazon DynamoDB)
- Model Executor (Wasmtime sandbox, WebAssembly scoring models)
- Audit Dispatcher (`aws-sdk-rust`, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Kinesis Firehose)
- Model Registry Client (AWS KMS, Amazon S3)
- Container Infrastructure (Amazon ECS Fargate, AWS API Gateway, Internal ALB)

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Routes screening requests [Internal ALB / gRPC]
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store & Cache: Performs low-latency feature lookups [TCP/TLS with mTLS]
- Model Registry Client -> Model Storage: Fetches signed Wasm binaries [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Audit Dispatcher -> Audit & Streaming Pipeline: Emits decision payloads [AWS SDK / HTTP/2]

## Technology Stack
- Rust (Tokio): Chosen for memory safety and zero garbage collection pauses to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Provides a managed container runtime within the fixed 25,000 EUR monthly infrastructure budget.
- WebAssembly (Wasm) via Wasmtime: Enables isolated, secure model execution and zero-downtime hot-reloading via atomic pointers (`ArcSwap`).
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis & DynamoDB: Deliver high-throughput, low-latency feature retrieval.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit retention.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Rust on ECS Fargate to reliably achieve sub-50ms latency at high throughput within a lean 3-engineer team constraint. Strict zero-trust networking, memory zeroization, and sandboxed Wasm execution ensure full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and auditable security.

Case Management App.analysis:
## Overview
[The Case Management App enables fraud analysts and compliance officers to review suspicious payment transactions, manage cases, and execute audit checks. It balances rapid analyst workflows with strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a €25k/month AWS budget constraint.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst
- Risk / Compliance Officer
- Case API Controller (TypeScript / NestJS)
- Case Orchestrator Service (TypeScript)
- Audit & Evidence Proxy (TypeScript)
- Feedback & Telemetry Emitter (TypeScript)
- Case & Audit Read Store (Amazon DynamoDB)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock)
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams / Firehose)
- Identity Provider / IdP (OIDC/OAuth2)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Case API Controller: Reviews cases and manages screening workflows [HTTPS / mTLS]
- Compliance Officer -> Case API Controller: Inspects audit trails and logs read-only [HTTPS / mTLS]
- Case API Controller -> Case Orchestrator Service: Dispatches workflow commands [In-memory function calls]
- Case Orchestrator Service -> Case & Audit Read Store: Reads and updates case state [HTTPS / AWS SDK via VPC Endpoints]
- Audit & Evidence Proxy -> Case & Audit Read Store: Queries tamper-evident decision logs and model explanations [HTTPS / AWS SDK via VPC Endpoints]
- Feedback & Telemetry Emitter -> Audit & Streaming Pipeline: Streams analyst feedback tags for offline model retraining [HTTPS / Kinesis API]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript / NestJS: Chosen for rapid UI-driven feature delivery and low operational overhead for a three-person engineering team.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Container orchestration platform ensuring zero server management within the fixed infrastructure budget.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Indexed read store for fast, secure audit retrieval and case caching without direct S3 query overhead.
- Zod / class-validator: Strict schema validation library for input sanitization and preventing injection vulnerabilities in the analyst UI.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secure runtime storage and automatic rotation for IdP tokens and database connection strings.

## Rationale
[This architecture fits the requirements by utilizing serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a three-person team while enforcing robust security, RBAC/ABAC controls, and tamper-evident auditing. Decoupling audit queries via DynamoDB and routing telemetry through resilient pipelines ensures sub-second analyst workflows remain uninterrupted and compliant with PCI-DSS Level 1.]

Feature Store & Cache.analysis:
## Overview
[Feature Store & Cache] provides real-time, low-latency feature lookups and profile storage for the payment fraud scoring engine, ensuring sub-50ms transaction evaluations while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
* Feature Retrieval API / Router (Rust / Node.js)
* Hot Cache Layer (Amazon ElastiCache Serverless Redis)
* Historical Feature Store (Amazon DynamoDB on-demand)
* Cache Invalidation & Sync Worker (Rust)

## Relationships
* Scoring Engine -> Hot Cache Layer: Retrieves real-time aggregates and hot features via TCP / RESP with TLS 1.3
* Scoring Engine -> Historical Feature Store: Queries wider entity profiles via AWS SDK over HTTPS/2
* Audit & Streaming Pipeline -> Cache Invalidation & Sync Worker: Ingests feature/rule state updates via Amazon Kinesis Consumer (TCP/HTTP) in under 1 second

## Technology Stack
* Amazon ElastiCache Serverless Redis: Provides sub-millisecond hot feature retrieval with zero operational scaling toil to meet the R-04 performance SLA within budget
* Amazon DynamoDB on-demand: Stores historical entity profiles with automated point-in-time recovery (PITR) to satisfy reliability constraints without cluster sizing overhead
* AWS KMS: Encrypts data at rest using Customer Managed Keys with annual rotation to fulfill PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates
* AWS IAM: Enforces strict least-privilege access and database authentication to secure internal component boundaries

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless AWS primitives to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while easily sustaining 3,000 TPS under the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Furthermore, strict VPC isolation, tokenization, and TLS 1.3 enforce necessary PCI-DSS security compliance and auditability.

Audit & Streaming Pipeline.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for suspicious payments. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Shopper / Cardholder, Merchant, Fraud Analyst, Risk / Compliance Officer
- AWS API Gateway
- Scoring Engine (Rust (Tokio), Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Case Management App (Node.js/Python, Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Feature Store & Cache (Amazon ElastiCache Redis, Amazon DynamoDB)
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Kinesis Firehose, AWS Lambda)
- Audit Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- Audit DLQ (Amazon SQS)

## Relationships
- Shopper / Cardholder -> Merchant: Initiates card-not-present payment [HTTPS]
- Merchant -> AWS API Gateway: Submits authorization requests [HTTPS/REST]
- AWS API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Routes payment payloads [HTTP/2]
- Scoring Engine -> Feature Store & Cache: Queries user profiles and fraud rules [Redis RESP / DynamoDB API]
- Scoring Engine -> Audit & Streaming Pipeline: Streams pre-redacted audit events [AWS SDK / Kinesis PutRecords API]
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline -> Audit Storage: Persists immutable audit logs [AWS internal storage APIs]
- Audit & Streaming Pipeline -> Audit DLQ: Routes poisoned or failed records [AWS SQS SDK]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management App: Reviews flagged payments [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Low-overhead HTTP/2 ingress for processing 3,000 TPS.
- Rust (Tokio) & Amazon ECS Fargate: High-performance, low-latency execution for the Scoring Engine to meet the <50ms P99 SLA.
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & Firehose: Scalable ingestion and batching for streaming audit logs.
- Amazon S3 (Object Lock Compliance Mode): Ensures 7-year tamper-evident storage for regulatory compliance.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed keys with automatic rotation for PCI-DSS data encryption.

## Rationale
The architecture combines low-latency containerized compute with fully managed AWS streaming and storage services to process 3,000 TPS under 50ms P99. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability while operating within a €25,000 monthly budget for a three-person engineering team.

Audit Storage.analysis:
## Overview
[The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations, enabling secure automated decisions and analyst reviews. It ensures strict 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS compliance within a fixed budget.]

## Key Elements
- S3 Bucket (Data Partition)
- S3 Object Lock Policy Engine
- AWS Glue Data Catalog
- Athena Query Interface
- S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

## Relationships
- Risk / Compliance Officer -> Athena Query Interface: Queries historical audit logs [HTTPS/Console, SQL]
- Athena Query Interface -> S3 Bucket (Data Partition): Scans immutable audit records [AWS internal storage APIs]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Ensures tamper-evident 7-year retention for R-06 compliance
- AWS KMS: Encrypts audit data at rest using Customer Managed Keys with annual rotation
- Amazon Athena & AWS Glue Data Catalog: Enables serverless SQL querying over partitioned audit logs
- S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval: Optimizes long-term storage costs to fit the 25,000 EUR monthly budget

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies strict 7-year audit and PCI-DSS mandates while maintaining low operational overhead for a 3-engineer team. Cloud tiering and serverless querying balance cost constraints with rapid compliance retrieval capabilities.]
